name: Arcturus VMG-4 'Turret'
description:
A retractable 7.62mm machine gun mounted in a concealed housing beneath the roof or hood of a standard passenger vehicle. The VMG-4 deploys in 1.5 seconds from its housing, rises on a motorized gimbal, and provides 180-degree forward arc fire controlled by the vehicle's onboard targeting system or by a gunner operating through a dashboard-mounted display. The weapon fires standard 7.62mm NATO at 800 RPM from a 200-round belt contained in the vehicle's chassis, and retracts flush after engagement, leaving no visible trace of the weapon's existence.

Arcturus sells the VMG-4 as an executive protection package — an integrated vehicle defense system that transforms any sedan or SUV into a light combat platform without external modification. The weapon's concealment is its primary feature: a VMG-4-equipped vehicle looks identical to every other vehicle on the road until the moment the roof panel slides open and a machine gun emerges. This moment tends to resolve traffic disputes with finality.

The VMG-4's integration with vehicle systems extends beyond the weapon itself. The targeting system ties into the vehicle's forward-facing cameras, radar, and LIDAR, providing aim assistance and target tracking that compensates for vehicle motion. An operator can engage targets while driving at highway speed, with the fire control system adjusting for velocity, target movement, and lead. The result is a mobile weapons platform that looks like a luxury sedan.
legality: Restricted — executive protection license with vehicle weapons permit
specifications:
caliber: 7.62x51mm NATO
rate of fire: 800 RPM
feed: 200-round belt (chassis-mounted)
deployment time: 1.5 seconds
arc of fire: 180 degrees forward
weight: 35 kg (weapon and housing)
mounting: Concealed roof or hood housing
tactical_use: Mobile vehicle defense and offensive engagement from concealment. The VMG-4 provides surprise firepower in ambush scenarios, convoy protection, and executive extraction operations. The weapon's concealment means the first indication of its presence is 7.62mm rounds arriving at the target.
cultural_context: The VMG-4 has contributed to a specific paranoia in GLMZ's traffic culture — the awareness that any vehicle might be armed. Aggressive driving takes on new implications when the car you just cut off might have a machine gun in its roof. Traffic courtesy in GLMZ's upper tiers is driven as much by survival instinct as by politeness.
known_users: Wealthy individuals with vehicle weapons permits
Confirmed use by at least three criminal organizations
story_hooks: A VMG-4 was deployed on a public highway during what appeared to be a road rage incident — 200 rounds of 7.62mm fired into traffic, killing four people in three vehicles. The shooter's vehicle was registered to a corporate executive who claims it was stolen 20 minutes before the incident.

A mechanic has discovered a VMG-4 installed in a vehicle brought in for routine service — the owner didn't know it was there. Someone installed a concealed machine gun in a civilian vehicle without the owner's knowledge, and the weapon is loaded and live.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, brutalist machine gun assembly designed for flush mounting. The weapon itself is utilitarian and angular — a feeding system and barrel assembly with minimal aesthetic pretense, dominated by its motorized gimbal housing that resembles a reinforced spherical joint. When retracted, only a recessed panel outline is visible beneath vehicle paneling; when deployed, the gun rises on a articulated arm like a turret emerging from armor plating.
physical_description.dimensions: Weapon assembly: 48cm length, 22cm width, 18cm height. Motorized gimbal housing: 35cm diameter spherical enclosure. Deployment height above vehicle roof: 32cm when fully raised.
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial and deliberately overbuilt — 35kg total feels dense and immovable when mounted. The gimbal assembly has mechanical heft that speaks to precision engineering and load-bearing capacity. Individual components are modular and heavy enough to require proper mounting, not a retrofit afterthought.
physical_description.primary_material: Hardened steel for the barrel and feed system. Titanium-reinforced polymer composite for the housing enclosure and gimbal structure. Internal mechanisms are precision-machined aluminum alloy.
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial gray with deliberate wear-resistant coating. The barrel shows a slightly darker oxide finish. Housing panels have a textured non-reflective surface treatment designed to prevent optical detection. Internal mechanisms visible through the gimbal joint feature brushed steel with light surface oxidation from factory testing.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with charcoal black internal components. Faint industrial orange accent markings on safety interlocks and calibration points. Chrome-plated securing bolts at gimbal joints.
physical_description.grip_texture: Not applicable — weapon is vehicle-mounted. Fire control is entirely electronic via dashboard interface or remote gunner station.
distinctive_features: Spherical motorized gimbal housing with three-axis articulation points
Recessed optical pickup ports for targeting system integration
Articulated feed arm that extends as weapon deploys
Four heavy-duty mounting tabs designed for flush roof/hood installation
Emergency manual traverse wheel on gimbal side for manual fire control
Heat dissipation vents that only appear when weapon is raised
Integrated pressure-relief valves for rapid retraction pneumatics
Segmented panel design that retracts flush when powered down
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Ironside Armaments logo stamped on gimbal housing (small, 4cm). Serial plate mounted on the feed system arm showing model 'VMG-4', manufacturing date, and caliber designation. Small regulatory compliance stamps on mounting brackets indicating vehicle weapons permit requirements.
physical_description.condition_typical: Factory-pristine when installed, showing minimal field wear due to the weapon being housed and retracted. Professional maintenance is required; operators typically see only the gimbal housing assembly during routine checks. Battle-worn examples show scuffing on the exterior panels, occasional dents on the housing from near-impacts, and scorching around the muzzle brake from sustained fire. Well-maintained executive protection vehicles show no visible wear — cosmetic condition is identical to factory spec.
